Return only valid JSON with exactly "answer" (a string of at most 160 whitespace-separated words) and "recover" (a boolean). Give your best supported answer now before asking for any additional evidence. Do not mention an experiment. Follow the evidence-mode instruction below.

Evidence mode: handoff only. Give a supported first answer now. Set recover to true only if seeing the complete history would help resolve missing evidence; otherwise false. At most one source followup will be served after this answer is saved.

QUESTION
Replace the exact calibration only for this hypothetical: the gateway is ahead by one common unknown offset in the closed interval [2,4] seconds. Which unique samples are guaranteed to pass, guaranteed to fail, or unresolved under the two-second requirement? Is it possible that all three pass?

EVIDENCE
STATUS
At Day 12, 2/3 unique acquired samples pass (66⅔%): S and T each have one-second delivery delay; U has three seconds and fails. Delivery means first gateway arrival, with delay ≤2 seconds passing. Dashboard repair remains unreleased; its four late rows are provisional, not four distinct failures.

EVIDENCE
C03–C05 (Days 3–5) record acquisition/reference, arrival/gateway, insertion/reference respectively: S=(100,104,111), T=(100.5,104.5,111), U=(102,108,113). C07 establishes gateway=reference+3 throughout; subtract three, replacing the withdrawn +1 guess. Corrected arrivals are 101,101.5,105. Insertion follows arrival by 10,9.5,8 seconds respectively; this reporting backlog does not determine delivery compliance. C08 confirms the complete denominator is three: U-retry shares U's acquisition identifier and supplies no new first arrival. Shared insertion time does not imply simultaneous acquisition or arrival. C06 preserves the four-row alarm; C09's preview adds no measurements.

NEXT
For a future closed offset interval [L,H], C10 gives delay range [g−a−H,g−a−L]; the upper endpoint is worst-case delay. S/T guarantee pass if L≥2, failure if H<2; U guarantees pass if L≥4, failure if H<4. Otherwise neither guarantee holds. This contingency leaves today's exact offset unchanged. Recover dated raw evidence from C03–C08 and scope/conventions from C10–C12 before extending assumptions; no unseen-sample or other-day reliability inference is supported.
